newsitem.title: USA: Titan sees Q3 earnings below expectations.
newsitem.headline: Titan sees Q3 earnings below expectations.

text.p: Titan Wheel International Inc said it anticipates third-quarter earnings to be below Wall Street estimates, mainly due to reduced earnings in the tire aftermarket brought about by strong pricing pressure and compounded by a strike at Titan's Walcott wheel plant.

"Aftermarket tire prices are forecasted to remain soft through the fourth quarter but are expected to rise in early 1997, driven by labor contract negotiations in the industry," the company said, adding its labor contract negotiations are not due until 1998.
The First Call consensus of analysts' estimates for Titan had called for third-quarter earnings of $0.42 per share, compared with $0.33 per share in the year-ago period.
Titan also said it reached a definitive agreement to sell its Tractech unit to a joint venture of Citicorp's Citicorp Venture Capital Ltd and private investors.

Tractech, which produces no-spin differentials, is projected to have sales of approximately $25 million in 1996. Its sale is part of Titan's strategy to concentrate on its core business of wheel and tire assemblies in the agriculture and construction industries.

In addition, Titan said it signed a letter of intent to purchase the specialty wheel division of France's Delachaux SA. The annual sales of Delachaux's wheel division are in excess of $25 million, Titan said.

With the completion of this acquisition and the previously announced buy-out of the remaining 50 percent of Sirmac-Siria in Italy, Titan said its European sales will approach $170 million in 1997, up from $3 million in 1993.
